name: Can pool resurfacing fix a slippery pool surface?

mainEntity.name: If the pool surface feels slippery, will resurfacing solve it or make it worse?
mainEntity.text: If the pool surface feels slippery, will resurfacing solve it or make it worse?

acceptedAnswer.text: A slippery pool surface can sometimes be corrected with resurfacing, but the finish choice matters. Worn plaster and calcium scale can make a surface feel slick or glassy, while certain new finishes offer more texture and grip. Pebble and some aggregate surfaces typically provide better traction than polished or very smooth finishes. However, resurfacing is not a substitute for water balance and algae control. If the slipperiness is caused by residue, buildup, or poor chemistry, a new finish alone will not solve it permanently. Homeowners should ask contractors which finishes are best for comfort and traction, especially around steps, benches, and shallow entries. If safety is a concern, it is worth requesting sample boards or references on how a finish feels underfoot once cured.
acceptedAnswer.description: Resurfacing can improve traction if the old surface is worn smooth or coated with scale, but some finishes are naturally more textured than others. Pebble and certain aggregate surfaces usually provide more grip than polished plaster. The wrong finish choice can still feel slippery if the pool is poorly maintained or algae is present.
